sources.limits: The overview supplies regional connections but sparse labels; the two enlarged windows supply readable river and neighboring-feature labels. correspondence: The complete selected one-piece mainstem and its distinct extent were inspected. The western of the two separately recorded neighboring Greenland model paths. It begins near 69.36°N around 37.8°W, runs southwest into a long near-southward interior line around 38.1°W, shifts west through the middle course and finishes after a short irregular marginal segment near 66.36°N. No separate tributary fragment is selected. These directional and shape statements describe the generalized model, not an observed natural channel.

The original geological sheet, readable graticule and southeastern regional pixels place the long upper and middle route within the mapped Inland Ice. The southern continuation approaches the southeastern glaciated margin north of the Tasiilaq/Ammasalik coastal setting. It has a near-straight southward upper-middle leg, a small westward step around the 67.4°N sector and another very long north–south lower-interior leg. The final short curved portion approaches the glaciated northern Tasiilaq-region margin. It is separate from the slightly more easterly hydro-system:90103860 selection.

No natural-river hydronym is established for the complete selected ice-sheet line. The nearby coastal place names and any outlet-glacier or fjord context cannot name the long modeled interior route. A completed feature-class/name-scope hold is supported; it does not imply that every natural marginal or subglacial watercourse lacks a name.

The inspected original Inland Ice legend and retained descriptive bulletin distinguish ice-surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments south of 68°N. These map symbols are not evidence of a continuously flowing named river along the model. The historical mapped ice margin is not treated as a contemporary observation.

correspondence.finding: The actual eastern beginning follows a small stream setting east into an elongated lake, then continues east through a branching stream-and-small-lake landscape. It turns south at the eastern lake-bearing corridor and passes a sequence of larger connected lake settings. These features and their connecting valleys are visible on the original upper map. The modeled straight connectors are generalized and locally offset from channels and shorelines; they do not define surveyed through-lake routes or a formal river source. No individual lake or feeder name is established by the inspected pixels.

Below the prominent eastern lake chain, the selected valley trends south and then southwest. It follows the mapped stream through the southern canyon-and-bend sequence before entering the Hornaday corridor at the southwestern junction. The receiving trunk is directly labeled Hornaday River. The map separately labels a southern continuation toward the Erly Lake surroundings as Hornaday River; that branch and Erly Lake are unselected, and the model does not establish its eastern approach as the uniformly named upper Hornaday.

From the southern connection, the selected line turns northwest and north along the repeatedly labeled Hornaday River, through the broad-to-confined valley and its large middle bends. Both detail windows overlap on this named trunk. East-side tributary valleys and nearby large lake waters remain distinct. In particular, Parks Canada identifies Little Hornaday River as a tributary reached from Hornaday Lake; that general description is not used to assign either name to the selected eastern feeder without a direct map label.

The lower selection follows the northward Hornaday valley and then its westward and northwestward canyon course through the Melville Hills. Repeated labels lie along the actual selected corridor. Rummy Lake lies in a separate western lake-and-stream setting; Seven Islands Lake and Brock River are east and northeast of the selected lower route. Neither the lake settings nor Brock River is substituted for the selected river.

After the final lower bend, the selection follows the Hornaday delta setting east of Paulatuk, with Rat Lake separately labeled nearby. Its endpoint lies in the coastal delta/mouth setting rather than on a route across open coastal water. Parks Canada independently describes Hornaday River reaching the Arctic Ocean east of Paulatuk. The generalized line does not establish the exact active distributary, current shoreline, tidal boundary or formally defined mouth point.

The initial modeled route starts in the lake-and-wetland country east of Mary Lake, first goes southeast through the southern lake complex, then turns north toward the Red Wine Lake vicinity. It continues west and north on a tributary approach before joining the east/northeast upper-river corridor south of Rainbow Hill. The selected beginning is therefore not replaced by the conventional Marie Lake/Smallwood headwater account. No name is assigned to this southern feeder, and Mary Lake is a neighboring reference rather than a claimed selected passage.

After the western junction the selection follows the northeast-trending valley through the Caribou Lake setting, then the eastward Wuchusk Lake corridor. The separate Kanairiktok route and Blake–Hall lake corridor lie northwest; Thomas River and its lake chain lie south. The provincial Wuchusk station explicitly identifies the Naskaupi inflow at the west side of Wuchusk and its continuation toward Grand Lake.

The selection continues from Wuchusk east and southeast into the eastern Seal Lake setting, then south through Naskaupi Lake and the downstream winding valley. It does not traverse the long western arms of Seal/Upper Seal Lake or the separate Namaycush–Portage lake branch to the northeast. The Naskaupi-below-lake profile supports the named river immediately downstream of Naskaupi Lake and distinguishes the Wapustan tributary.

The middle fragment follows the continuous southeast-trending Naskaupi valley below the upper lake district. The regional cartography distinguishes side-valley arrivals from the principal corridor; the historical fisheries account describes the Wapustan, North Pole and lower Red Wine waterways as tributaries, not alternative names for the whole selected line. No tributary fragments are included in this object.

The final fragment continues down the Naskaupi past its lower western tributary approach into the northern end of Grand Lake. Crooked River is a distinct neighboring arrival from the northeast/east and is not the selected upstream corridor. Both the historical river account and the provincial station description locate the Naskaupi mouth at Grand Lake.

After reaching Grand Lake, the selected line runs a substantial distance southeast inside the lake to its outlet. It then passes through the Little Lake setting and the short North West River outlet near the two communities to the Lake Melville margin. The provincial Grand Lake outflow profile explicitly describes Grand Lake draining via the Rapids into Little Lake and then through North West River into Lake Melville. These lake interiors and the separately named outlet are not a uniform continuation of the Naskaupi hydronym.

The retained 1985 fisheries account and provincial profiles document diversion of former Naskaupi headwaters into the Churchill system. That history does not establish contemporary flow at every modeled upper connection or make the current modeled start the official source. The research result is regional identity and component scope, not an operational flow assessment or an official river-length claim.

correspondence: The complete selected one-piece mainstem and its distinct extent were inspected. The eastern of the two separately recorded neighboring Greenland model paths. It begins near 69.4°N around 37.5°W, descends south-southwest, follows a long near-southward middle leg, shifts southwest below that leg and ends in the glaciated margin near 66.43°N. No separate tributary fragment is selected. These directional and shape statements describe the generalized model, not an observed natural channel.

The original geological sheet, readable graticule and southeastern regional pixels place the long upper and middle route within the mapped Inland Ice. The southern continuation approaches the southeastern glaciated margin north of the Tasiilaq/Ammasalik coastal setting. It retains a narrow north–south interior corridor east of the neighboring hydro-system:90104636, with a southwestward lower bend followed by short near-vertical terminal legs. The selections approach different modeled terminal positions and are not merged or treated as alternate IDs for one named natural river.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
